QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_79

question.text: A trader's initial margin deposit is Rs. 1,00,000 for a futures position. After MTM losses of Rs. 35,000, the margin balance drops to Rs. 65,000. If the maintenance margin is 75% of initial margin, what happens?

answer.text: The margin balance (Rs. 65,000) is below the maintenance margin (Rs. 75,000), so the trader receives a margin call to bring the balance back to the initial margin of Rs. 1,00,000
Nothing happens because the margin balance is still positive at Rs. 65,000
The trader's position is automatically squared off at the next day's opening
The exchange waives the margin shortfall since it is less than 50% of the initial margin

explanation.text: The Logic: When a futures position takes an MTM loss, the client's margin balance is debited. In a standard maintenance-margin framework, once the balance falls below a stipulated maintenance level (here 75% of the initial margin, i.e. Rs. 75,000), a margin call is issued. The client is required to top up the account back to the initial margin level (Rs. 1,00,000) — in this case by depositing Rs. 35,000. If the client fails to deposit the notional loss within the stipulated time, the broker may liquidate the position wholly or partly. The Trap: A positive balance alone is not sufficient — what matters is whether it is above the maintenance threshold. The position is not auto-squared off the next morning before any call is issued, and exchanges do not waive shortfalls on a percentage basis. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (160, 202) support initial margin, MTM losses, the requirement to deposit the notional loss within the stipulated time and the broker's right to liquidate on default, but the specific 75% maintenance-margin threshold, the "margin call" terminology, and "restore to initial margin" wording were not located in the pages checked. The framing above reflects general futures-margin mechanics rather than a direct workbook citation.
